text: I really think that we're just starting into this golden era of what it might mean to be a writer on the internet. The economic model for supporting great writing on the internet has been generally pretty terrible for the entirety of the internet's history.
speaker: Sachin Monga
context: Sachin is discussing his long-term vision for where Substack is heading as a product. He's explaining how the internet has historically failed to properly compensate quality writers, but Substack is changing this landscape. He mentions that beyond established writers like Matt Taibbi who joined early, there are now many newer writers finding success who don't even identify primarily as writers but are making substantial income from their work.
text_ko: 저는 우리가 이제 막 인터넷에서 작가로 산다는 것의 의미가 새롭게 정의되는 황금기에 접어들기 시작했다고 정말 생각해요. 그동안 인터넷 역사 전반에 걸쳐 훌륭한 글을 경제적으로 뒷받침하는 모델은 대체로 형편없었어요.
text_zh: 我真心觉得，我们才刚刚开始进入网络写作者的黄金时代，才开始弄清楚在网上写作到底意味着什么。支持优秀网络写作的经济模式 (economic model) 在互联网的整个历史里一直都很差。
text_es: Creo que apenas estamos empezando a entrar en lo que podría ser una edad de oro para ser escritor en internet. El modelo económico para financiar la escritura de calidad en internet ha sido, en general, bastante deficiente durante casi toda la historia de internet.
key_sentence: We're starting into a golden era of what it means to be a writer.
original_text: I really think that we're just starting into this golden era of what it might mean to be a writer on the internet. The economic model for supporting great writing on the internet has been generally pretty terrible for the entirety of the internet's history. But in the last year or so, even in the last few months, I think there's been so many really interesting success stories now from writers who might not even consider themselves writers.

vocabulary.definition: An economic model is a theoretical construct that represents economic processes through a set of variables and logical relationships. It is used to analyze and predict economic behavior and outcomes.
vocabulary.businessContext: In business and tech, economic models are essential for understanding market dynamics, pricing strategies, and the financial viability of new ventures or products.
vocabulary.nuance: While 'economic model' can refer to various frameworks, it is often used in discussions about sustainability and profitability in business strategies.

vocabulary.definition: Supporting refers to the act of providing assistance, resources, or validation to help someone or something succeed. It can involve emotional, financial, or logistical aid.
vocabulary.businessContext: In a business context, supporting often relates to backing initiatives, projects, or employees to enhance productivity and morale.
vocabulary.nuance: The term can imply a secondary role, suggesting that the subject is not the primary focus but is essential for success.

text: We're still pretty early, but we have something going now.
speaker: Sachin Monga
context: Lenny asks Sachin about how Substack's product team is structured and how it might evolve as they scale. Sachin explains that when he joined Substack a year ago, they had zero product managers, but they've now built out a proper product organization. He describes their current structure of three full-stack teams aligned around different user types rather than product features.
text_ko: 아직 초반이긴 하지만, 지금은 뭔가 잘 돌아가고 있어요.
text_zh: 我们还在起步阶段，不过现在已经开始有起色了。
text_es: Todavía estamos en una fase muy temprana, pero ya tenemos algo en marcha.
key_sentence: We're still pretty early, but we have something going now.
original_text: We're still pretty early, but we have something going now. We have four product managers in addition to myself, and we have three essentially kind of full stack product teams now that have a PM and an engineering manager, a data person or a designer, engineers and things are starting to roll. We're finally emerging from this transition phase and it's been super fun.

text: I think the first thing was really treating my role in the beginning more as a facilitator than a decision maker when it comes to product. When I first joined, I felt like my main role was actually just solving that.
speaker: Sachin Monga
context: Lenny asks about the challenge of being a head of product at a small company with a founder who has strong product opinions. Sachin explains his approach to working with Chris, Substack's CEO. Rather than trying to be the primary decision maker immediately, Sachin focused on being a bridge between Chris and the product teams, ensuring clear communication of vision and priorities as the company grew beyond the point where Chris could be involved in every decision.
text_ko: 처음에는 제품(product)에 관해서 제 역할을 의사결정자(decision maker)라기보다 조율자(facilitator)로 보는 게 맞다고 생각했어요. 합류했을 때는 제 주된 역할이 사실 그 부분을 해결하는 것뿐이라고 느꼈어요.
text_zh: 关于产品，我一开始更把自己当成推动者(facilitator)，而不是决策者(decision maker)。刚加入那会儿，我觉得自己主要的工作就是把这事儿处理好。
text_es: Creo que al principio enfoqué mi rol más como facilitador que como quien toma las decisiones sobre el producto (product). Cuando me uní, sentía que mi papel principal era precisamente resolver eso.
key_sentence: Treating my role as a facilitator was my main role in the beginning.
original_text: I think the first thing was really treating my role in the beginning more as a facilitator than a decision maker when it comes to product. When I first joined, I felt like my main role was actually just solving that. And if nothing else, if Chris could have a really good sense of what all the teams are doing and if the teams knew where he was coming from and could start to get better at modeling him and his vision, that would be a win.

vocabulary.definition: A facilitator is an individual who helps a group of people understand their common objectives and assists them in achieving those goals by guiding discussions and processes.
vocabulary.businessContext: In business settings, facilitators often lead meetings, workshops, or training sessions to ensure productive collaboration and effective communication among team members.
vocabulary.nuance: The term implies a supportive role rather than a directive one, emphasizing collaboration over authority.

vocabulary.definition: A decision maker is a person who has the authority to make choices or determine a course of action within an organization.
vocabulary.businessContext: In corporate environments, decision makers are typically senior executives or managers who evaluate options and make strategic decisions that impact the direction of the company.
vocabulary.nuance: This term carries a connotation of responsibility and authority, often implying a higher level of accountability for outcomes.

vocabulary.definition: Solving refers to the process of finding a solution to a problem or addressing a challenge.
vocabulary.businessContext: In the context of business and technology, solving often involves analytical thinking and creative problem-solving skills to overcome obstacles and improve processes.
vocabulary.nuance: This term suggests an active engagement in overcoming difficulties, often requiring critical thinking and resourcefulness.

text: Maybe that leads into my answer to the second question, which is that's not really for everyone. I think there's almost like a personality type that has to be okay with being humbled all the time and feeling like you don't know what you're doing.
speaker: Sachin Monga
context: Lenny asks about what type of person isn't a good fit for the role of head of product at a fast-growing startup with a product-minded founder. Sachin explains that the constant change and growth at startups means processes become obsolete quickly, requiring someone comfortable with uncertainty. He contrasts this with working at more stable companies where you can master established processes and systems.
text_ko: 아마 그게 두 번째 질문에 대한 제 답으로 이어지는 것 같아요. 근데 그건 모든 사람에게 맞는 건 아니에요. 늘 겸손해지고 내가 뭘 하는지 모른다는 기분을 계속 견뎌낼 수 있는 성향이 있어야 해요.
text_zh: 这大概就是我对第二个问题的回答：这并不适合每个人。我觉得这更像是一种性格——得能接受不断被打击，常常觉得自己不太知道自己在干什么。
text_es: Quizá eso me lleva a la respuesta de la segunda pregunta: no es para todo el mundo. Creo que se necesita casi un tipo de personalidad que esté bien con que te pongan en evidencia todo el tiempo y con la sensación de no saber qué estás haciendo.
key_sentence: Being humbled all the time is necessary for this trajectory.
original_text: Maybe that leads into my answer to the second question, which is that's not really for everyone. I think there's almost like a personality type that has to be okay with being humbled all the time and feeling like you don't know what you're doing. I think you could be an amazing product manager at a company that is a bit more stable and consistent and get really good at what you're doing and someone who's going to be really good at a company that is on a bit of this trajectory, it's kind of a different job.

vocabulary.definition: A classification of individuals based on their characteristic patterns of thinking, feeling, and behaving. Different personality types can influence how individuals interact with others and approach challenges.
vocabulary.businessContext: In business settings, understanding personality types can enhance team dynamics, improve communication, and inform leadership styles, particularly in roles that require collaboration and conflict resolution.
vocabulary.nuance: While often used in team-building and recruitment contexts, it is important to avoid overgeneralizing individuals based on personality types, as this can lead to stereotyping.

vocabulary.definition: Feeling a sense of modesty or insignificance, often as a result of a challenging experience or realization. It can also refer to being brought down to a lower status or position.
vocabulary.businessContext: In the business world, being humbled can foster resilience and adaptability, as leaders and employees learn from failures and setbacks, ultimately leading to personal and professional growth.
vocabulary.nuance: While 'humbled' often has a positive connotation of growth, it can also imply a loss of confidence, so context is crucial when using the term.

text: writers are in control over being able to deliver their best work on their terms to their audience, make money directly from their subscribers, and also that readers should be in control over their experience.
speaker: Sachin Monga
context: Lenny asks how Substack prioritizes what to work on and what their North Star is. Sachin explains that Substack's founders start from core principles about how the internet should work, with people having control over their own destiny rather than being subject to algorithmic feeds. This principle of user control - both for writers and readers - guides their product decisions and prioritization framework.
text_ko: 작가들은 자신이 원하는 방식으로 최고의 작품을 독자들에게 전달할 주도권을 가지고, 구독자(subscribers)에게서 직접 수익을 얻을 수 있어야 해요. 동시에 독자들(readers)도 자신의 경험을 스스로 선택하고 통제할 수 있어야 해요.
text_zh: 作者可以自己掌控，按自己的方式把最好的作品呈现给受众、直接从订阅者(subscribers)那里赚钱；同时读者也能掌控自己的阅读体验。
text_es: Que los escritores puedan ofrecer lo mejor de su trabajo en sus propias condiciones a su audiencia, generar ingresos directamente de sus suscriptores y que, además, los lectores tengan el control de su experiencia.
key_sentence: Writers are in control of delivering their best work on their terms.
original_text: When you think about what that means for Substack right now, that that means writers are in control over being able to deliver their best work on their terms to their audience, make money directly from their subscribers, and also that readers should be in control over their experience. When you show up to Substack.com, that experience should be something that you have a much greater degree of agency over or if you download the app than if you maybe opened up TikTok or something.

vocabulary.definition: The power to influence or direct behavior or the course of events.
vocabulary.businessContext: In a business context, control can refer to management's ability to steer operations, maintain quality standards, and ensure compliance with regulations.
vocabulary.nuance: While control implies authority, it can also suggest a balance between oversight and empowerment, particularly in collaborative environments.

text: What if we just ask writers, who do you recommend? What if we just put that in the subscribe flow and just made it as simple as possible?
speaker: Sachin Monga
context: Sachin is explaining how Substack's recommendation feature came to be. Rather than building an algorithmic system like Facebook's 'People You May Know', they decided to give writers full control by simply asking them who they recommend. Chris initially worried this approach would be difficult to execute because it required multiple steps - writers opting in, making good choices, and the system generating enough exposure for the recommendations to be meaningful.
text_ko: 작가분들한테 그냥 ‘누구 추천하세요?’라고 물어보면 어떨까요? 그걸 구독 플로우(subscribe flow)에 넣고 최대한 단순하게 만들면 어떨까요?
text_zh: 要不我们直接问作者：“你推荐谁？”然后把这件事放到订阅流程(subscribe flow)里，尽量简化，怎么样？
text_es: ¿Y si simplemente les preguntamos a los escritores: "¿A quién nos recomiendan?" ¿Y si lo incluimos en el flujo de suscripción (subscribe flow) y lo dejamos lo más sencillo posible?
key_sentence: What if we just ask writers, who do you recommend?
original_text: What if we just ask writers, who do you recommend? What if we just put that in the subscribe flow and just made it as simple as possible? I think Chris' reaction to that originally when that idea came up was that's probably just going to be really hard to pull off. There's a lot more things that have to be true. You need writers to opt in. You need to pick good people. You need to find a way to surface those recommendations to the readers in a way that's going to generate a good amount of surface area.

vocabulary.definition: To suggest or endorse a course of action, product, or service based on one's judgment or experience.
vocabulary.businessContext: In business settings, recommending products or services can influence customer decisions and enhance sales strategies, often seen in marketing and customer service interactions.
vocabulary.nuance: While 'recommend' implies a positive endorsement, it should be used carefully to avoid overstepping into manipulation or bias.

vocabulary.definition: A structured process through which users can sign up for a service or content, often involving a series of steps or prompts.
vocabulary.businessContext: In tech and startup environments, optimizing the subscribe flow is crucial for user acquisition and retention, as it directly impacts conversion rates.
vocabulary.nuance: The term suggests a seamless and user-friendly experience; a poorly designed subscribe flow can deter potential users.

text: My first piece of advice would be to just start it and see what happens. Start it. Have a way to start gathering subscribers. Put a link to it somewhere. Write one or two things.
speaker: Sachin Monga
context: Lenny asks what advice Sachin has for writers thinking about starting a newsletter or joining Substack. Sachin emphasizes the importance of simply beginning rather than overthinking the process. He suggests that people experiment with different content formats and leverage any existing audience they might have on other platforms, viewing it as a way to gain more control over their relationship with their audience.
text_ko: 제 첫 번째 조언은 그냥 시작해 보고 어떻게 되는지 지켜보라는 거예요. 일단 시작하세요. 구독자(subscribers)를 모을 수 있는 방법을 마련해 두고, 어딘가에 링크를 걸어 두세요. 그리고 한두 개 정도 글을 써 보세요.
text_zh: 我的第一个建议就是先开始，别想太多，看看会怎样。先上线，想办法开始拉订阅者(subscribers)。把链接放到某个地方，先写一两篇内容就行。
text_es: Mi primer consejo sería: simplemente ponlo en marcha y ve qué pasa. Ponlo en marcha. Ten alguna forma de empezar a captar suscriptores. Pon un enlace en algún sitio. Escribe una o dos cosas.
key_sentence: just start it and see what happens.
original_text: My first piece of advice would be to just start it and see what happens. Start it. Have a way to start gathering subscribers. Put a link to it somewhere. Write one or two things. If you're not much of a writer, try posting a video, recording some audio, turn into a little podcast. Just start basically and see what happens and see what kind of interest there might be out there for what you have to say, especially if you already have a following on other platforms as well.

vocabulary.definition: The act of collecting or assembling items, people, or information together for a specific purpose.
vocabulary.businessContext: In business, gathering often refers to the collection of data, feedback, or resources necessary for decision-making or project development.
vocabulary.nuance: While 'gathering' can imply a casual collection, in a business context it often suggests a structured approach to collecting valuable insights or resources.

vocabulary.definition: Individuals or entities that have opted to receive regular updates, content, or services from a provider, often in exchange for a fee or free of charge.
vocabulary.businessContext: In the tech and startup sectors, subscribers are crucial for building a customer base and generating revenue through subscription models or newsletters.
vocabulary.nuance: The term 'subscribers' carries a connotation of commitment, suggesting that these individuals have a vested interest in the content or services offered.
